say: Can empty space make something from nothing?

Empty space is never truly empty. Pairs of particles flicker into being, and vanish again.
But at the edge of a black hole, one of the pair can fall in, [0.3] while the other escapes.
That glow is real: Hawking radiation, predicted in nineteen seventy-four, but still too faint to detect.
But it isn't free. [0.4] ~Each escaping particle is paid for with the black hole's own mass.
A black hole as heavy as the Sun would need ten to the sixty-seven years to evaporate. [0.3] ~The universe is just thirteen point eight billion years old.
So even at the edge of a black hole, nothing is really free.
